deficiency_causes__thiamine.subject: thiamine
deficiency_causes__thiamine.source: Thiamine deficiency affects the cardiovascular, nervous, and immune systems and commonly manifests as wet beriberi, dry beriberi, or Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome.

classic_finding__thiamine.subject: thiamine
classic_finding__thiamine.source: Wernicke encephalopathy is an acute, time-sensitive neurologic disorder caused by thiamine deficiency that requires prompt recognition and treatment to prevent irreversible neurologic damage.

deficiency_causes__niacin.subject: niacin
deficiency_causes__niacin.source: Niacin (vitamin B3) deficiency results in a condition known as pellagra.

classic_finding__niacin.subject: niacin
classic_finding__niacin.source: Niacin deficiency results in pellagra, which includes the triad or "three Ds," dermatitis, dementia, and diarrhea, and can result in death.

deficiency_causes__cobalamin.subject: cobalamin
deficiency_causes__cobalamin.source: As a result, homocysteine levels accumulate, and pyrimidine bases cannot be formed, slowing down DNA synthesis and can cause megaloblastic anemia.

classic_finding__cobalamin.subject: cobalamin
classic_finding__cobalamin.source: Subacute combined degeneration (SCD) of the spinal cord is a disease affecting the lateral and posterior columns of the spinal cord, primarily due to demyelination. It most commonly presents in patients deficient in vitamin B12, producing hematological and neurological manifestations. This condition is most commonly caused by vitamin B12 deficiency.

deficiency_causes__folate.subject: folate
deficiency_causes__folate.source: Reduced folate levels result in a decreased availability of THF, which impairs purine and pyrimidine synthesis and nucleoprotein metabolism. This disruption results in ineffective erythropoiesis, megaloblastic anemia, and impaired cellular proliferation.

classic_finding__folate.subject: folate
classic_finding__folate.source: Folate deficiency has a well-established teratogenic effect, leading to an increasing risk of neural tube defects.

deficiency_causes__vitamin_c.subject: vitamin_c
deficiency_causes__vitamin_c.source: Scurvy is a clinical syndrome resulting from vitamin C deficiency.

classic_finding__vitamin_c.subject: vitamin_c
classic_finding__vitamin_c.source: Proline residues on procollagen require vitamin C for hydroxylation, making it necessary for the triple-helix formation of mature collagen.

deficiency_causes__vitamin_d.subject: vitamin_d
deficiency_causes__vitamin_d.source: Deficiency of this beneficial substance can lead to nutritional rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

classic_finding__vitamin_d.subject: vitamin_d
classic_finding__vitamin_d.source: Deficiency of this beneficial substance can lead to nutritional rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

deficiency_causes__vitamin_a.subject: vitamin_a
deficiency_causes__vitamin_a.source: Night blindness or defective vision in dim light is the earliest clinical manifestation of Vitamin A deficiency.

classic_finding__vitamin_a.subject: vitamin_a
classic_finding__vitamin_a.source: Xerophthalmia refers to the constellation of ocular signs and symptoms associated with Vitamin A deficiency. ... First, it may be caused by reduced dietary intake of Vitamin A, which is more often seen in developing countries.

deficiency_causes__vitamin_k.subject: vitamin_k
deficiency_causes__vitamin_k.source: Vitamin K deficiency causes a bleeding diathesis (coagulopathy).

classic_finding__vitamin_k.subject: vitamin_k
classic_finding__vitamin_k.source: Across age groups, vitamin K deficiency is characterized by impaired γ-carboxylation of clotting factors, leading to prolonged prothrombin time with normal platelet counts and fibrinogen levels.
